---
title: "Behavior"
subtitle: "Activity patterns, drinking behavior, and shade use under shade and water access treatments"
---

```{r setup}
#| include: false
#| cache: false   # options (emm_options) and packages must be set on every render

library(tidyverse)
library(lme4)
library(lmerTest)
library(emmeans)
library(ggplot2)
library(plotly)
library(rstatix)
library(knitr)
library(kableExtra)
library(readxl)
library(patchwork)
library(multcomp)
library(glmmTMB)
library(DHARMa)

select <- dplyr::select

# ── Denominator df for emmeans on LMMs ────────────────────────────────────────
# The experimental unit is group × period (16 units), so tests must use
# Satterthwaite df rather than asymptotic z (emmeans' default once n > 3000).
emm_options(lmer.df = "satterthwaite", lmerTest.limit = 1e5, pbkrtest.limit = 0)

# ── Model fitting with convergence / singularity handling ─────────────────────
# Fits the LMM (lmer) or, when `family` is given, the GLMM (glmer). On a
# convergence warning or singular fit, refits with bobyqa; if still singular,
# drops random terms with zero variance (never group:period) and records what
# was done in `model_log`, together with the final random-effect variances.
model_log <- tibble(model = character(), status = character(), action = character(),
                    final = character())

fit_mm <- function(formula, data, label, family = NULL) {
  f_txt <- paste(deparse(formula, width.cutoff = 500), collapse = " ")
  f_txt <- str_replace(f_txt, fixed("(1 | day/hour)"), "(1 | day) + (1 | day:hour)")
  ctrl_bobyqa <- if (is.null(family)) lmerControl(optimizer = "bobyqa") else glmerControl(optimizer = "bobyqa")
  fit <- function(f, ctrl = NULL) {
    msgs <- character()
    m <- withCallingHandlers(
      if (is.null(family)) {
        lmer(as.formula(f), data = data, control = ctrl %||% lmerControl())
      } else {
        glmer(as.formula(f), data = data, family = family, control = ctrl %||% glmerControl())
      },
      warning = function(w) { msgs <<- c(msgs, conditionMessage(w)); invokeRestart("muffleWarning") }
    )
    conv <- c(msgs, m@optinfo$conv$lme4$messages)
    list(m = m, conv = conv[!str_detect(conv, "singular")])
  }
  res    <- fit(f_txt)
  status <- c(if (length(res$conv)) "convergence warning", if (isSingular(res$m)) "singular")
  action <- character()
  if (length(status)) {
    res    <- fit(f_txt, ctrl_bobyqa)
    action <- "refit with bobyqa"
    if (isSingular(res$m)) {
      vc   <- as.data.frame(VarCorr(res$m))
      zero <- setdiff(vc$grp[vc$vcov < 1e-8], c("Residual", "group:period"))
      if (length(zero)) {
        for (z in zero) f_txt <- str_remove(f_txt, fixed(paste0(" + (1 | ", z, ")")))
        res    <- fit(f_txt, ctrl_bobyqa)
        action <- c(action, paste0("dropped zero-variance term(s): ", paste(zero, collapse = ", ")))
      }
      if (isSingular(res$m)) action <- c(action, "group:period variance ≈ 0 (retained by design)")
    }
    if (length(res$conv)) action <- c(action, paste("still:", paste(unique(res$conv), collapse = " / ")))
  }
  vc_final <- as.data.frame(VarCorr(res$m))
  model_log <<- bind_rows(model_log, tibble(
    model  = label,
    status = if (length(status)) paste(status, collapse = " + ") else "OK",
    action = if (length(action)) paste(action, collapse = "; ") else "—",
    final  = paste0(vc_final$grp, " = ", signif(vc_final$vcov, 3), collapse = "; ")
  ))
  res$m
}

# Records convergence of a glmmTMB fit (optimizer code + positive-definite Hessian)
log_tmb <- function(m, label) {
  ok <- m$fit$convergence == 0 && isTRUE(m$sdr$pdHess)
  vc <- unlist(lapply(VarCorr(m)$cond, function(v) v[1]))
  model_log <<- bind_rows(model_log, tibble(
    model  = label,
    status = if (ok) "OK" else "convergence problem",
    action = "glmmTMB (nlminb)",
    final  = paste0(names(vc), " = ", signif(vc, 3), collapse = "; ")
  ))
  invisible(m)
}

# ── Pearson dispersion ratio for count GLMMs ──────────────────────────────────
overdisp_fun <- function(model) {
  rdf <- df.residual(model)
  rp  <- residuals(model, type = "pearson")
  Pearson.chisq <- sum(rp^2)
  prat <- Pearson.chisq / rdf
  pval <- pchisq(Pearson.chisq, df = rdf, lower.tail = FALSE)
  c(chisq = Pearson.chisq, ratio = prat, rdf = rdf, p = pval)
}

# ── p-value formatting for inline text ────────────────────────────────────────
fmt_p <- function(p) ifelse(p < 0.001, "< 0.001", paste("=", formatC(p, format = "f", digits = 3)))

# ── Clock time labels (scan 1 = 07:00 … scan 24 = 06:00) ─────────────────────
scan_to_clock <- function(scan) {
  hour_val <- (scan + 6) %% 24
  sprintf("%02d:00", hour_val)
}
clock_labels <- setNames(scan_to_clock(1:24), 1:24)
day_labels   <- clock_labels[1:12]
night_labels <- clock_labels[13:24]

# ── Convert scans/h to % of scans (6 scans per hour) ─────────────────────────
scan_to_pct <- function(x) round(x / 6 * 100, 1)

# ── Theme ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
theme_ws <- function(angle_x = 0) {
  theme_classic(base_family = "sans", base_size = 12) +
    theme(
      plot.title         = element_text(face = "bold", color = "#2C4A2E", size = 13),
      plot.subtitle      = element_text(color = "#6B6B6B", size = 11),
      axis.title         = element_text(color = "#2A2A2A", size = 11),
      axis.text          = element_text(color = "#2A2A2A"),
      axis.text.x        = element_text(angle = angle_x,
                                        hjust = if (angle_x > 0) 1 else 0.5),
      legend.title       = element_text(face = "bold", size = 10),
      legend.position    = "bottom",
      panel.grid.major.y = element_line(color = "#DDD5C4", linewidth = 0.4),
      strip.background   = element_rect(fill = "#F5F0E8", color = "#DDD5C4"),
      strip.text         = element_text(face = "bold", color = "#2C4A2E")
    )
}

# ── emmeans helper (LMM) ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────
emm_table <- function(model, factor_name) {
  emm  <- emmeans(model, as.formula(paste("~", factor_name)))
  cont <- pairs(emm, adjust = "tukey")

  emm_raw <- as.data.frame(emm)
  emm_df  <- data.frame(
    Level = emm_raw[[1]],
    Mean  = round(emm_raw$emmean, 3),
    SE    = round(emm_raw$SE,     3)
  )

  cont_raw <- as.data.frame(cont)
  cont_df  <- data.frame(
    Comparison = cont_raw$contrast,
    Estimate   = round(cont_raw$estimate, 4),
    SE_c       = round(cont_raw$SE,       4),
    `t / z`    = round(if ("t.ratio" %in% names(cont_raw)) cont_raw$t.ratio else cont_raw$z.ratio, 4),
    `p-value`  = round(cont_raw$p.value,  4),
    check.names = FALSE
  )
  cont_df$Sig <- dplyr::case_when(
    cont_df$`p-value` < 0.001 ~ "***",
    cont_df$`p-value` < 0.01  ~ "**",
    cont_df$`p-value` < 0.05  ~ "*",
    cont_df$`p-value` < 0.1   ~ ".",
    TRUE                       ~ "ns"
  )
  list(means = emm_df, contrasts = cont_df)
}

# ── emmeans helper on the response scale (log-LMM, Poisson / NB GLMMs) ────────
# Means are back-transformed (geometric means for a log response; rates for
# count models) and the contrast is a ratio.
emm_response_table <- function(model, factor_name) {
  emm  <- emmeans(model, as.formula(paste("~", factor_name)), type = "response")
  emm_raw  <- as.data.frame(emm)
  cont_raw <- as.data.frame(pairs(emm, adjust = "tukey"))
  lcl <- intersect(c("lower.CL", "asymp.LCL"), names(emm_raw))[1]
  ucl <- intersect(c("upper.CL", "asymp.UCL"), names(emm_raw))[1]
  emm_df <- data.frame(
    Level    = emm_raw[[1]],
    Response = round(emm_raw[[2]], 3),
    SE       = round(emm_raw$SE, 3),
    LCL      = round(emm_raw[[lcl]], 3),
    UCL      = round(emm_raw[[ucl]], 3)
  )
  stat <- intersect(c("t.ratio", "z.ratio"), names(cont_raw))[1]
  cont_df <- data.frame(
    Comparison = cont_raw$contrast,
    Ratio      = round(cont_raw$ratio, 4),
    SE_c       = round(cont_raw$SE, 4),
    `t / z`    = round(cont_raw[[stat]], 4),
    `p-value`  = round(cont_raw$p.value, 4),
    check.names = FALSE
  )
  list(means = emm_df, contrasts = cont_df)
}

# ── Data loading ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
behavior_raw <- read_excel("data/behavior.xlsx") %>%
  mutate(
    treatment  = factor(treatment, levels = c("S+W+", "S+W-", "S-W+", "S-W-")),
    breed      = factor(breed),
    animal_id  = factor(animal_id),
    group      = factor(group),
    day        = as.factor(day),
    period     = as.factor(period),
    hour       = as.integer(hour),
    location   = factor(location,
                        levels = c("sun", "shade", "sun_between_trees",
                                   "open_sun", "night")),
    clock_time = scan_to_clock(hour),
    daypart    = if_else(hour <= 12, "Daytime", "Nighttime")
  )

# ── Aggregated behavioral data (one row per animal × day × hour) ──────────────
# Behavioral categories:
#   grazing             = grazing only (pure grazing; "other" is no longer added)
#   other               = other behaviors (analysed as a separate category)
#   lying               = lying_idle + lying_ruminating (reviewer's "resting")
#   standing            = idle + ruminating (posture standing, excl. grazing/other)
#   ruminating_tot      = ruminating + lying_ruminating (any posture)
behavior <- behavior_raw %>%
  group_by(treatment, group, breed, animal_id, period, day, hour, clock_time, daypart) %>%
  summarise(
    grazing          = sum(grazing,          na.rm = TRUE),
    idle             = sum(idle,             na.rm = TRUE),
    lying_idle       = sum(lying_idle,       na.rm = TRUE),
    ruminating       = sum(ruminating,       na.rm = TRUE),
    lying_ruminating = sum(lying_ruminating, na.rm = TRUE),
    other            = sum(other,            na.rm = TRUE),
    total            = sum(total,            na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    shade          = factor(if_else(str_detect(as.character(treatment), "S\\+"), "S+", "S-"),
                            levels = c("S+", "S-")),
    water          = factor(if_else(str_detect(as.character(treatment), "W\\+"), "W+", "W-"),
                            levels = c("W+", "W-")),
    lying          = lying_idle + lying_ruminating,            # posture
    standing       = idle + ruminating,                        # posture
    ruminating_tot = ruminating + lying_ruminating,            # activity any posture
    daypart        = factor(daypart, levels = c("Daytime", "Nighttime"))
  )

behavior_day   <- behavior %>% filter(daypart == "Daytime")
behavior_night <- behavior %>% filter(daypart == "Nighttime")

# ── Drinking event data ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────
drinking <- read_excel("data/water_intake_behavior.xlsx") %>%
  mutate(
    treatment = factor(treatment, levels = c("S+W+", "S+W-", "S-W+", "S-W-")),
    animal_id = factor(animal_id),
    group     = factor(group),
    period    = factor(period),
    day       = as.factor(day),
    hour      = as.factor(hour),
    shade     = factor(if_else(str_detect(as.character(treatment), "S\\+"), "S+", "S-"),
                       levels = c("S+", "S-")),
    water     = factor(if_else(str_detect(as.character(treatment), "W\\+"), "W+", "W-"),
                       levels = c("W+", "W-"))
  )

# Daily drinking events per animal. count() alone drops animal-days with zero
# events, so counts are joined onto the complete animal × day grid (every
# animal on both collection days of every period, with its group's treatment)
# and missing animal-days are filled with 0.
animal_day_grid <- behavior %>%
  distinct(animal_id, group, period, day, treatment, shade, water)

events <- animal_day_grid %>%
  mutate(across(c(animal_id, day), as.character)) %>%
  left_join(
    drinking %>%
      mutate(across(c(animal_id, day), as.character)) %>%
      count(animal_id, day, name = "events"),
    by = c("animal_id", "day")
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    events    = replace_na(events, 0L),
    animal_id = factor(animal_id),
    day       = factor(day, levels = levels(behavior$day))
  )

# ── Water intake data ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
intake <- read_excel("data/water_intake.xlsx") %>%
  mutate(
    treatment         = factor(treatment, levels = c("S+W+", "S+W-", "S-W+", "S-W-")),
    group             = factor(group),
    period            = factor(period),
    day               = factor(day),
    intake_per_animal = intake_L / 8,
    shade             = factor(if_else(str_detect(as.character(treatment), "S\\+"), "S+", "S-"),
                               levels = c("S+", "S-")),
    water             = factor(if_else(str_detect(as.character(treatment), "W\\+"), "W+", "W-"),
                               levels = c("W+", "W-"))
  )
```

# 1 · Daily Activity Budget

```{r}
#| code-summary: "Daily activity budget — mutually exclusive behaviors by treatment and period"

budget_tbl <- behavior %>%
  group_by(treatment, daypart, animal_id) %>%
  summarise(
    n_scans = sum(total, na.rm = TRUE),
    across(c(grazing, lying_idle, lying_ruminating,
             idle, ruminating, other), ~ sum(., na.rm = TRUE)),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  mutate(across(grazing:other, ~ . / n_scans)) %>%
  group_by(treatment, daypart) %>%
  summarise(across(grazing:other, ~ round(mean(.) * 100, 1)), .groups = "drop") %>%
  rename(
    Treatment         = treatment,
    Daypart           = daypart,
    `Grazing (%)`     = grazing,
    `Lying idle (%)`  = lying_idle,
    `Lying rum. (%)`  = lying_ruminating,
    `Standing idle (%)` = idle,
    `Standing rum. (%)` = ruminating,
    `Other (%)`       = other
  )

budget_tbl %>%
  kbl(caption = "Table 1. Mean proportion of behavioral scans (%) by treatment and period.") %>%
  kable_styling(bootstrap_options = c("striped", "hover"), full_width = FALSE) %>%
  row_spec(0, background = "#2C4A2E", color = "white", bold = TRUE)
```

```{r}
#| code-summary: "Daily activity budget — stacked bar by treatment and period"
#| fig-cap: "Figure 1. Mean proportion of behavioral scans by treatment and period. Each bar sums to 100%."

budget_long <- behavior %>%
  group_by(treatment, daypart, animal_id) %>%
  summarise(
    n_scans = sum(total, na.rm = TRUE),
    across(c(grazing, lying_idle, lying_ruminating,
             idle, ruminating, other), ~ sum(., na.rm = TRUE)),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  mutate(across(grazing:other, ~ . / n_scans)) %>%
  group_by(treatment, daypart) %>%
  summarise(across(grazing:other, mean), .groups = "drop") %>%
  pivot_longer(grazing:other, names_to = "behavior", values_to = "proportion") %>%
  mutate(behavior = factor(behavior,
    levels = c("grazing", "lying_idle", "lying_ruminating",
               "idle", "ruminating", "other")))

p_budget <- ggplot(budget_long,
                   aes(x = treatment, y = proportion, fill = behavior)) +
  geom_col(position = "fill", width = 0.75) +
  scale_fill_manual(
    values = c(
      "grazing"          = "#2C4A2E",
      "lying_idle"       = "#4A7FA5",
      "lying_ruminating" = "#7BADC8",
      "idle"             = "#C8A84B",
      "ruminating"       = "#DDB96B",
      "other"            = "#DDD5C4"
    ),
    labels = c("Grazing", "Lying idle", "Lying ruminating",
               "Standing idle", "Standing ruminating", "Other")
  ) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::percent) +
  facet_wrap(~ daypart) +
  labs(x = "Treatment", y = "Proportion of scans", fill = "Behavior") +
  theme_ws()

ggplotly(p_budget, tooltip = c("x", "y", "fill")) %>%
  layout(legend = list(orientation = "h", x = 0, y = -0.2))
```

# 2 · Daytime Behavioral Categories

## 2.1 · Grazing

::: {.panel-tabset}

### By treatment

```{r}
#| code-summary: "LMM — daytime grazing by treatment"

model_graz_day_trat <- fit_mm(
  grazing ~ treatment + period + (1 | group) + (1 | group:period) + (1 | animal_id) + (1 | day / hour),
  data = behavior_day, label = "model_graz_day_trat"
)

graz_day_trat_emm <- emm_table(model_graz_day_trat, "treatment")

graz_day_trat_emm$means %>%
  rename(Treatment = Level) %>%
  kbl(caption = "Table 2. Estimated marginal means — daytime grazing by treatment.",
      digits = 3) %>%
  kable_styling(bootstrap_options = c("striped", "hover"), full_width = FALSE) %>%
  row_spec(0, background = "#2C4A2E", color = "white", bold = TRUE)

graz_day_trat_emm$contrasts %>%
  kbl(caption = "Table 3. Pairwise contrasts — daytime grazing by treatment.",
      digits = 4) %>%
  kable_styling(bootstrap_options = c("striped", "hover"), full_width = FALSE) %>%
  row_spec(0, background = "#2C4A2E", color = "white", bold = TRUE)
```

```{r}
#| code-summary: "Daytime grazing by treatment — box plot"
#| fig-cap: "Figure 2. Daytime grazing (scans/h) by treatment."

p_graz_trat <- ggplot(behavior_day,
                      aes(x = treatment, y = grazing, fill = treatment)) +
  geom_boxplot(alpha = 0.7, outlier.shape = 21, outlier.size = 1.5) +
  geom_jitter(width = 0.15, alpha = 0.2, size = 1) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = pal_treatment) +
  labs(x = "Treatment", y = "Grazing scans / h (daytime)", fill = NULL) +
  theme_ws() +
  theme(legend.position = "none")

ggplotly(p_graz_trat, tooltip = c("x", "y"))
```

```{r}
#| code-summary: "LMM — nocturnal lying, ruminating, standing, and other by treatment"

model_lying_night_trat <- fit_mm(
  lying ~ treatment + period + (1 | group) + (1 | group:period) + (1 | animal_id) + (1 | day / hour),
  data = behavior_night, label = "model_lying_night_trat"
)

model_rum_night_trat <- fit_mm(
  ruminating_tot ~ treatment + period + (1 | group) + (1 | group:period) + (1 | animal_id) + (1 | day / hour),
  data = behavior_night, label = "model_rum_night_trat"
)

model_stand_night_trat <- fit_mm(
  standing ~ treatment + period + (1 | group) + (1 | group:period) + (1 | animal_id) + (1 | day / hour),
  data = behavior_night, label = "model_stand_night_trat"
)

model_other_night_trat <- fit_mm(
  other ~ treatment + period + (1 | group) + (1 | group:period) + (1 | animal_id) + (1 | day / hour),
  data = behavior_night, label = "model_other_night_trat"
)

lying_night_trat_emm <- emm_table(model_lying_night_trat, "treatment")
rum_night_trat_emm   <- emm_table(model_rum_night_trat,   "treatment")
stand_night_trat_emm <- emm_table(model_stand_night_trat, "treatment")
other_night_trat_emm <- emm_table(model_other_night_trat, "treatment")

# EMM tables for the four nocturnal behaviors
bind_rows(
  lying_night_trat_emm$means %>% mutate(Behavior = "Lying"),
  rum_night_trat_emm$means   %>% mutate(Behavior = "Ruminating"),
  stand_night_trat_emm$means %>% mutate(Behavior = "Standing"),
  other_night_trat_emm$means %>% mutate(Behavior = "Other")
) %>%
  rename(Treatment = Level) %>%
  select(Behavior, Treatment, Mean, SE) %>%
  kbl(caption = "Estimated marginal means — nocturnal behaviors by treatment.",
      digits = 3) %>%
  kable_styling(bootstrap_options = c("striped", "hover"), full_width = FALSE) %>%
  row_spec(0, background = "#2C4A2E", color = "white", bold = TRUE)
```

# 4 · 24-hour Behavioral Profile

```{r}
#| code-summary: "Full 24h profile of grazing, lying, standing, and ruminating"
#| fig-cap: "Figure 17. Mean scans per hour across the full 24-hour cycle by treatment. Dashed line marks the daytime–nighttime transition (19:00h). Ruminating (any posture) overlaps with lying and standing."

full_ts <- behavior %>%
  group_by(treatment, hour, clock_time) %>%
  summarise(
    Grazing    = mean(grazing,        na.rm = TRUE),

    Ruminating = mean(ruminating_tot, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  pivot_longer(c(Grazing, Lying, Standing, Ruminating),
               names_to = "behavior", values_to = "mean") %>%
  mutate(clock_time = factor(clock_time, levels = clock_labels))

p_full_ts <- ggplot(full_ts,
                    aes(x = hour, y = mean,
                        color = behavior, group = behavior)) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 12.5, linetype = "dashed",
             color = "#6B6B6B", linewidth = 0.7) +
  annotate("text", x = 6.5,  y = max(full_ts$mean, na.rm = TRUE) * 0.96,
         label = "Daytime",   hjust = 0.5, size = 3, color = "#6B6B6B") +
  annotate("text", x = 18.5, y = max(full_ts$mean, na.rm = TRUE) * 0.96,
         label = "Nighttime", hjust = 0.5, size = 3, color = "#6B6B6B") +
  geom_line(linewidth = 1) +
  geom_point(size = 1.8) +
  scale_color_manual(values = c(
    "Grazing"    = "#2C4A2E",
    "Lying"      = "#4A7FA5",
    "Standing"   = "#C8A84B",
    "Ruminating" = "#6B4C35"
  )) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = 1:24, labels = unname(clock_labels)) +
  facet_wrap(~ treatment, nrow = 2) +
  labs(x = "Clock time", y = "Mean scans / h", color = "Behavior") +
  theme_ws(angle_x = 45)

ggplotly(p_full_ts, tooltip = c("x", "y", "color")) %>%
  layout(legend = list(orientation = "h", x = 0.35, y = -0.15))
```

# 5 · Drinking Behavior and Water Intake

## 5.1 · Drinking Frequency

Daily drinking events are counted on the complete animal × day grid: every animal on both collection days of its period, with animal-days without any drinking event entered as 0.

```{r}
#| code-summary: "Poisson GLMM — drinking events by water group (zero days included)"

model_events <- fit_mm(
  events ~ water + period + (1 | group) + (1 | group:period) + (1 | animal_id) + (1 | day),
  data = events, family = poisson, label = "model_events (Poisson)"
)

# ── Dispersion check (Pearson) ────────────────────────────────────────────────
overdisp <- overdisp_fun(model_events)

overdisp_tbl <- tibble(
  Metric = c("Animal-days (incl. zero days)", "Animal-days with zero events",
             "Pearson chi-square", "Residual df", "Dispersion ratio", "p-value (overdispersion)"),
  Value  = c(nrow(events), sum(events$events == 0),
             round(overdisp["chisq"], 2),
             round(overdisp["rdf"],   0),
             round(overdisp["ratio"], 3),
             formatC(overdisp["p"], format = "e", digits = 2))
)

overdisp_tbl %>%
  kbl(caption = "Table 32. Dispersion diagnostics for the Poisson GLMM of daily drinking events.") %>%
  kable_styling(bootstrap_options = c("striped", "hover"), full_width = FALSE) %>%
  row_spec(0, background = "#2C4A2E", color = "white", bold = TRUE)

emm_events  <- emmeans(model_events, ~ water, type = "response")
cont_events <- pairs(emm_events, adjust = "tukey")

emm_events_df <- as.data.frame(emm_events) %>%
  rename(`Water group` = water, Rate = rate) %>%
  select(`Water group`, Rate, SE, asymp.LCL, asymp.UCL) %>%
  mutate(across(where(is.numeric), ~ round(., 3)))

cont_events_df <- as.data.frame(cont_events) %>%
  rename(Comparison = contrast, `Rate ratio` = ratio,
         SE_c = SE, `z` = z.ratio, `p-value` = p.value) %>%
  select(Comparison, `Rate ratio`, SE_c, `z`, `p-value`) %>%
  mutate(
    across(where(is.numeric), ~ round(., 4)),
    Sig = case_when(
      `p-value` < 0.001 ~ "***",
      `p-value` < 0.01  ~ "**",
      `p-value` < 0.05  ~ "*",
      `p-value` < 0.1   ~ ".",
      TRUE               ~ "ns"
    )
  )

emm_events_df %>%
  kbl(caption = "Table 33. Back-transformed estimated means — drinking events/day by water group.",
      digits = 3) %>%
  kable_styling(bootstrap_options = c("striped", "hover"), full_width = FALSE) %>%
  row_spec(0, background = "#2C4A2E", color = "white", bold = TRUE)

cont_events_df %>%
  kbl(caption = "Table 34. Contrast — drinking events W+ vs W− (rate ratio).", digits = 4) %>%
  kable_styling(bootstrap_options = c("striped", "hover"), full_width = FALSE) %>%
  row_spec(0, background = "#2C4A2E", color = "white", bold = TRUE)
```

```{r}
#| code-summary: "Sensitivity check — generalized Poisson GLMM (glmmTMB) if underdispersed"

# A dispersion ratio clearly below 1 (< 0.8) means the Poisson model overstates
# the variance, so a generalized Poisson model is fitted as a sensitivity check.
events_underdispersed <- overdisp["ratio"] < 0.8

if (events_underdispersed) {
  model_events_gp <- glmmTMB(
    events ~ water + period + (1 | group) + (1 | group:period) + (1 | animal_id) + (1 | day),
    data   = events,
    family = genpois
  )
  log_tmb(model_events_gp, "model_events (generalized Poisson)")
  cont_events_gp <- as.data.frame(pairs(emmeans(model_events_gp, ~ water, type = "response")))
  emm_events_gp  <- as.data.frame(emmeans(model_events_gp, ~ water, type = "response"))

  events_sens_tbl <- tibble(
    Model        = c("Poisson (glmer)", "Generalized Poisson (glmmTMB)"),
    `Rate W+`    = c(emm_events_df$Rate[1], emm_events_gp$rate[1]),
    `Rate W−`    = c(emm_events_df$Rate[2], emm_events_gp$rate[2]),
    `Rate ratio` = c(cont_events_df$`Rate ratio`[1], cont_events_gp$ratio[1]),
    `p-value`    = c(cont_events_df$`p-value`[1], cont_events_gp$p.value[1]),
    `Dispersion (genpois φ)` = c(NA, sigma(model_events_gp)),
    AIC          = c(AIC(model_events), AIC(model_events_gp))
  ) %>%
    mutate(across(where(is.numeric), ~ round(., 4)))

  events_sens_tbl %>%
    kbl(caption = "Table 34a. Sensitivity check — Poisson vs generalized Poisson GLMM for daily drinking events.") %>%
    kable_styling(bootstrap_options = c("striped", "hover"), full_width = FALSE) %>%
    row_spec(0, background = "#2C4A2E", color = "white", bold = TRUE)
} else {
  cat("Dispersion ratio =", round(overdisp["ratio"], 3),
      "— not clearly below 1; the generalized Poisson sensitivity fit was not required.")
}
```

```{r}
#| code-summary: "Drinking events — mean ± SE with individual observations by treatment"
#| fig-cap: "Figure 18. Drinking events per animal per day by treatment (animal-days with no drinking events included as 0). Points are individual animal-day observations; diamonds and bars show group mean ± SE."

events_summary_plot <- events %>%
  group_by(treatment, water) %>%
  summarise(
    mean = mean(events),
    se   = sd(events) / sqrt(n()),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

p_events <- ggplot(events, aes(x = treatment, color = treatment)) +
  geom_jitter(aes(y = events), width = 0.15, height = 0.1, alpha = 0.45,
              size = 2.5, shape = 16) +
  geom_pointrange(
    data = events_summary_plot,
    aes(y = mean, ymin = mean - se, ymax = mean + se),
    shape = 18, size = 0.9, linewidth = 1.1, color = "black"
  ) +
  scale_color_manual(values = pal_treatment) +
  labs(x = "Treatment", y = "Drinking events / animal / day", color = NULL) +
  theme_ws() +
  theme(legend.position = "none")

ggplotly(p_events, tooltip = c("x", "y"))
```

## 5.2 · Daily Water Intake

Water intake was measured per group and day (group intake ÷ 8), so the model has no animal term: group and group × period are random, and day within group × period is the residual.

```{r}

)
```

## 5.3 · Drinking Bout Characteristics

::: {.panel-tabset}

### Drinking duration

Drinking duration is right-skewed, so it is modelled on the log scale; estimated means are back-transformed and are therefore **geometric means**, and the contrast is a ratio of geometric means.

```{r}
#| code-summary: "LMM — log drinking duration by water group (geometric means)"

model_drink_time <- fit_mm(
  log(drinking_time_s) ~ water + period + (1 | group) + (1 | group:period) + (1 | animal_id) + (1 | day),
  data = drinking, label = "model_drink_time (log)"
)

drink_time_emm <- emm_response_table(model_drink_time, "water")

drink_time_emm$means %>%
  rename(`Water group` = Level, `Geometric mean duration (s)` = Response) %>%
  kbl(caption = "Table 37. Back-transformed estimated marginal means (geometric means) — drinking duration by water group.",
      digits = 2) %>%
  kable_styling(bootstrap_options = c("striped", "hover"), full_width = FALSE) %>%
  row_spec(0, background = "#2C4A2E", color = "white", bold = TRUE)

drink_time_emm$contrasts %>%
  rename(`Ratio of geometric means` = Ratio) %>%
  kbl(caption = "Table 38. Contrast — drinking duration W+ / W− (ratio of geometric means).", digits = 4) %>%
  kable_styling(bootstrap_options = c("striped", "hover"), full_width = FALSE) %>%
  row_spec(0, background = "#2C4A2E", color = "white", bold = TRUE)
```

### Sips per event

Sips per event is a count, so it is modelled with a Poisson GLMM; if the Pearson dispersion ratio indicates overdispersion (ratio > 1.2 with p < 0.05), the model is refitted as a negative binomial GLMM (glmmTMB, `nbinom2`) and that model is reported.

```{r}
#| code-summary: "Poisson GLMM — sips per event by water group (NB2 if overdispersed)"

model_sips_pois <- fit_mm(
  sips ~ water + period + (1 | group) + (1 | group:period) + (1 | animal_id) + (1 | day),
  data = drinking, family = poisson, label = "model_sips (Poisson)"
)

overdisp_sips <- overdisp_fun(model_sips_pois)
sips_overdispersed <- overdisp_sips["ratio"] > 1.2 & overdisp_sips["p"] < 0.05

if (sips_overdispersed) {
  model_sips <- glmmTMB(
    sips ~ water + period + (1 | group) + (1 | group:period) + (1 | animal_id) + (1 | day),
    data   = drinking,
    family = nbinom2
  )
  log_tmb(model_sips, "model_sips (NB2)")
  sips_family <- "negative binomial (glmmTMB, nbinom2)"
} else {
  model_sips  <- model_sips_pois
  sips_family <- "Poisson (glmer)"
}

tibble(
  Metric = c("Pearson chi-square (Poisson)", "Residual df", "Dispersion ratio",
             "p-value (overdispersion)", "Model reported"),
  Value  = c(round(overdisp_sips["chisq"], 2), round(overdisp_sips["rdf"], 0),
             round(overdisp_sips["ratio"], 3), formatC(overdisp_sips["p"], format = "e", digits = 2),
             sips_family)
) %>%
  kbl(caption = "Table 38a. Dispersion diagnostics — sips per event.") %>%
  kable_styling(bootstrap_options = c("striped", "hover"), full_width = FALSE) %>%
  row_spec(0, background = "#2C4A2E", color = "white", bold = TRUE)

sips_emm <- emm_response_table(model_sips, "water")

sips_emm$means %>%
  rename(`Water group` = Level, `Mean sips / event` = Response) %>%
  kbl(caption = "Table 39. Back-transformed estimated marginal means — sips per event by water group.",
      digits = 2) %>%
  kable_styling(bootstrap_options = c("striped", "hover"), full_width = FALSE) %>%
  row_spec(0, background = "#2C4A2E", color = "white", bold = TRUE)

sips_emm$contrasts %>%
  rename(`Rate ratio` = Ratio) %>%
  kbl(caption = "Table 40. Contrast — sips per event W+ / W− (rate ratio).", digits = 4) %>%
  kable_styling(bootstrap_options = c("striped", "hover"), full_width = FALSE) %>%
  row_spec(0, background = "#2C4A2E", color = "white", bold = TRUE)
```

```{r}

                 aes(x = treatment, y = sips, fill = treatment)) +
```

# 6 · Shade Area Use (S+ Treatments)

Animals in S+ treatments had access to a silvopastoral area. Behavioral scans recorded each animal's location as shade (under tree canopy), sun between trees (silvopastoral area, not directly shaded), or sun (open pasture).

Note: Following the reviewer recommendation, the 12:00h observation was excluded from the analysis for **both** S+ treatments to avoid confounding with the scheduled watering removal of S+W− animals at that timepoint. The same applies to the 17:00h scan block, which contains the second watering window (17:30–18:00h): see the check below.

```{r}
#| code-summary: "Check — how S+W− animals are coded during the watering windows"

# W− animals were taken to the trough corridor at 12:00 and 17:30–18:00.
# The ethogram has no "corridor" location, so scans taken there can only be
# coded as sun or shade. Drinking events confirm when the W− groups drank.
watering_hours <- drinking %>%
  filter(water == "W-") %>%
  count(hour = as.integer(as.character(hour)), name = "w_minus_events") %>%
  slice_max(w_minus_events, n = 2) %>%
  pull(hour) %>% sort()

loc_check <- behavior_raw %>%
  filter(treatment %in% c("S+W+", "S+W-"), hour <= 12,
         location %in% c("sun", "shade", "sun_between_trees")) %>%
  group_by(treatment, hour, clock_time) %>%
  summarise(
    shade = sum(total[location == "shade"], na.rm = TRUE),
    sun   = sum(total[location != "shade"], na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  mutate(prop_shade = shade / (shade + sun)) %>%
  select(treatment, hour, clock_time, prop_shade, sun) %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = treatment, values_from = c(prop_shade, sun)) %>%
  mutate(diff = `prop_shade_S+W-` - `prop_shade_S+W+`)

loc_check %>%
  mutate(
    across(starts_with("prop_shade"), ~ scales::percent(., accuracy = 0.1)),
    diff = round(diff * 100, 1),
    `W− watering` = if_else(hour %in% watering_hours, "yes", "")
  ) %>%
  select(Time = clock_time, `Shade S+W+` = `prop_shade_S+W+`, `Shade S+W−` = `prop_shade_S+W-`,
         `Sun scans S+W+` = `sun_S+W+`, `Sun scans S+W−` = `sun_S+W-`,
         `S+W− − S+W+ (pp)` = diff, `W− watering`) %>%
  kbl(caption = "Table 42a. Daytime shade use of S+ animals by scan block (all scans), with the blocks in which the W− groups drank.") %>%
  kable_styling(bootstrap_options = c("striped", "hover"), full_width = FALSE) %>%
  row_spec(0, background = "#2C4A2E", color = "white", bold = TRUE)

# Scan blocks excluded from the shade-use model for both S+ treatments
shade_excluded_hours <- watering_hours
diff_noon <- round(loc_check$diff[loc_check$hour == watering_hours[1]] * 100, 1)
diff_pm   <- round(loc_check$diff[loc_check$hour == watering_hours[2]] * 100, 1)
diff_rest <- round(mean(loc_check$diff[!loc_check$hour %in% watering_hours]) * 100, 1)
```

W− animals drank in the `r clock_labels[watering_hours[1]]`h and `r clock_labels[watering_hours[2]]`h scan blocks (Table 42a). Because the ethogram has no corridor category, S+W− animals in the corridor were recorded as being in the sun: their shade use differed from S+W+ by `r diff_noon` percentage points at `r clock_labels[watering_hours[1]]`h and by `r diff_pm` points at `r clock_labels[watering_hours[2]]`h, against an average of `r diff_rest` points in the other daytime blocks. Both blocks (`r paste0(clock_labels[shade_excluded_hours], "h", collapse = " and ")`) are therefore excluded from the shade-use model for **both** S+ treatments. The scans are hourly totals, so the corridor scans cannot be separated from the rest of the block.

## 6.1 · Location Distribution Over Time

```{r}
#| code-summary: "Location use — scan distribution by treatment (daytime)"

shade_loc_tbl <- behavior_raw %>%
  filter(
    treatment %in% c("S+W+", "S+W-"),
    location  %in% c("sun", "shade", "sun_between_trees"),
    hour <= 12
  ) %>%
  group_by(treatment, location) %>%
  summarise(total_scans = sum(total, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop") %>%
  group_by(treatment) %>%
  mutate(
    `Proportion (%)` = round(total_scans / sum(total_scans) * 100, 1),
    location = recode(location,
      "shade"             = "Shade",
      "sun_between_trees" = "Sun between trees",
      "sun"               = "Sun")
  ) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  rename(Treatment = treatment, Location = location, Scans = total_scans)

shade_loc_tbl %>%
  kbl(caption = "Table 43. Daytime scan distribution (%) by location for S+ treatments.") %>%
  kable_styling(bootstrap_options = c("striped", "hover"), full_width = FALSE) %>%
  row_spec(0, background = "#2C4A2E", color = "white", bold = TRUE)
```

# 7 · Shade × Water Factorial Models

The four treatments form a 2 × 2 factorial (shade S+/S− × water W+/W−). The models below re-express the same comparisons as main effects of shade and water and their interaction, with the same random structure as the treatment models:

`y ~ shade * water + period + (1 | group) + (1 | group:period) + (1 | animal_id) + (1 | day/hour)`

Shade use is measured only in S+ animals and is therefore not included. Water intake is a group-day measure (no animal term), and the drinking bout models use `(1 | day)`; drinking events and sips per event use the same count families as in Section 5. *F* tests come from `emmeans::joint_tests()` (Satterthwaite df for LMMs; asymptotic df for GLMMs).

```{r}
#| code-summary: "Factorial models — shade × water for all outcomes"

re_beh  <- "+ period + (1 | group) + (1 | group:period) + (1 | animal_id) + (1 | day / hour)"
re_drk  <- "+ period + (1 | group) + (1 | group:period) + (1 | animal_id) + (1 | day)"

fact_specs <- tribble(
  ~key,              ~Outcome,                ~Daypart,    ~data,            ~resp,
  "graz_day",        "Grazing",               "Daytime",   "behavior_day",   "grazing",
  "other_day",       "Other",                 "Daytime",   "behavior_day",   "other",
  "lying_day",       "Lying",                 "Daytime",   "behavior_day",   "lying",
  "rum_day",         "Ruminating",            "Daytime",   "behavior_day",   "ruminating_tot",
  "stand_day",       "Standing",              "Daytime",   "behavior_day",   "standing",
  "graz_night",      "Grazing",               "Nighttime", "behavior_night", "grazing",
  "other_night",     "Other",                 "Nighttime", "behavior_night", "other",
  "lying_night",     "Lying",                 "Nighttime", "behavior_night", "lying",
  "rum_night",       "Ruminating",            "Nighttime", "behavior_night", "ruminating_tot",
  "stand_night",     "Standing",              "Nighttime", "behavior_night", "standing"
)

fact_models <- list()
for (i in seq_len(nrow(fact_specs))) {
  s <- fact_specs[i, ]
  fact_models[[s$key]] <- fit_mm(
    as.formula(paste(s$resp, "~ shade * water", re_beh)),
    data = get(s$data), label = paste0("factorial_", s$key)
  )
}

fact_models[["events"]] <- fit_mm(
  as.formula(paste("events ~ shade * water", re_drk)),
  data = events, family = poisson, label = "factorial_events (Poisson)"
)

fact_models[["intake"]] <- fit_mm(
  intake_per_animal ~ shade * water + period + (1 | group) + (1 | group:period),
  data = intake, label = "factorial_intake"
)

fact_models[["duration"]] <- fit_mm(
  as.formula(paste("log(drinking_time_s) ~ shade * water", re_drk)),
  data = drinking, label = "factorial_duration (log)"
)

if (sips_overdispersed) {
  fact_models[["sips"]] <- glmmTMB(
    as.formula(paste("sips ~ shade * water", re_drk)),
    data = drinking, family = nbinom2
  )
  log_tmb(fact_models[["sips"]], "factorial_sips (NB2)")
} else {
  fact_models[["sips"]] <- fit_mm(
    as.formula(paste("sips ~ shade * water", re_drk)),
    data = drinking, family = poisson, label = "factorial_sips (Poisson)"
  )
}

fact_models[["sip_rate"]] <- fit_mm(
  as.formula(paste("sip_rate_s ~ shade * water", re_drk)),
  data = drinking, label = "factorial_sip_rate"
)

fact_specs <- bind_rows(
  fact_specs,
  tribble(
    ~key,       ~Outcome,                         ~Daypart,
    "events",   "Drinking events / day (Poisson)", "24 h",
    "intake",   "Water intake (L/animal/day)",     "24 h",
    "duration", "Drinking duration (log s)",       "24 h",
    "sips",     paste0("Sips per event (", if (sips_overdispersed) "NB2" else "Poisson", ")"), "24 h",
    "sip_rate", "Sip rate (sips/s)",               "24 h"
  )
)

# ── joint_tests() for shade, water and shade:water ────────────────────────────
fact_jt <- map_dfr(fact_specs$key, function(k) {
  jt <- as.data.frame(joint_tests(fact_models[[k]]))
  jt %>%
    filter(`model term` %in% c("shade", "water", "shade:water")) %>%
    transmute(key = k, term = `model term`, df1, df2, F = F.ratio, p = p.value)
}) %>%
  left_join(fact_specs %>% select(key, Outcome, Daypart), by = "key")

fmt_F <- function(F, df1, df2) {
  df2_txt <- ifelse(is.infinite(df2), "∞", formatC(df2, format = "f", digits = 1))
  paste0("F(", df1, ", ", df2_txt, ") = ", formatC(F, format = "f", digits = 2))
}

fact_summary <- fact_jt %>%
  mutate(
    cell = paste0(fmt_F(F, df1, df2), "; p ",
                  ifelse(p < 0.001, "< 0.001", paste("=", formatC(p, format = "f", digits = 3))))
  ) %>%
  select(key, Outcome, Daypart, term, cell) %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = term, values_from = cell) %>%
  select(Outcome, Daypart, Shade = shade, Water = water, `Shade × Water` = `shade:water`)

fact_summary %>%
  kbl(caption = "Table 46. Shade × water factorial models — joint tests (F and p) for shade, water and their interaction.") %>%
  kable_styling(bootstrap_options = c("striped", "hover"), full_width = FALSE) %>%
  row_spec(0, background = "#2C4A2E", color = "white", bold = TRUE) %>%
  row_spec(which(fact_jt$p[fact_jt$term == "shade:water"] < 0.10), bold = TRUE) %>%
  footnote(general = "Rows in bold have a shade × water interaction with p < 0.10; their simple effects are shown in Table 47.")
```

```{r}
#| code-summary: "Simple effects where the shade × water interaction is p < 0.10"

int_keys <- fact_jt %>% filter(term == "shade:water", p < 0.10) %>% pull(key)

simple_effects <- map_dfr(int_keys, function(k) {
  m <- fact_models[[k]]
  is_resp <- k %in% c("events", "duration", "sips")
  one <- function(spec, by) {
    pr <- as.data.frame(pairs(emmeans(m, spec, type = if (is_resp) "response" else "link")))
    est_col <- intersect(c("ratio", "estimate"), names(pr))[1]
    stat    <- intersect(c("t.ratio", "z.ratio"), names(pr))[1]
    tibble(
      key        = k,
      Effect     = paste0(pr$contrast, " | ", by, " = ", pr[[by]]),
      Scale      = if (is_resp) "ratio" else "difference",
      Estimate   = pr[[est_col]],
      SE         = pr$SE,
      `t / z`    = pr[[stat]],
      `p-value`  = pr$p.value
    )
  }
  bind_rows(one(~ shade | water, "water"), one(~ water | shade, "shade"))
})

if (nrow(simple_effects)) {
  simple_effects %>%
    left_join(fact_specs %>% select(key, Outcome, Daypart), by = "key") %>%
    select(Outcome, Daypart, Effect, Scale, Estimate, SE, `t / z`, `p-value`) %>%
    mutate(across(where(is.numeric), ~ round(., 4))) %>%
    kbl(caption = "Table 47. Simple effects — shade within water level and water within shade level (outcomes with interaction p < 0.10).") %>%
    kable_styling(bootstrap_options = c("striped", "hover"), full_width = FALSE) %>%
    row_spec(0, background = "#2C4A2E", color = "white", bold = TRUE)
} else {
  cat("No outcome had a shade × water interaction with p < 0.10.")
}
```

# 8 · Experimental-Unit Sensitivity Analysis

Treatments were applied to whole groups for a whole period, so the 16 group × period cells are the true experimental units. As a check on the mixed models, every behavior, drinking and intake outcome was averaged to one value per group × period and analysed as a classic 4 × 4 Latin square:

`y ~ treatment + period + group` (lm; 15 − 9 = 6 error df), and `y ~ shade * water + period + group` (same 6 error df).

Cell means are the mean of all observations in the cell (animal-hours for behavior; animal-days for drinking events; group-days for intake; drinking bouts for duration, sips and sip rate). Duration is averaged on the log scale, as in the mixed model. Because treatment is orthogonal to group and period in a Latin square, sequential and adjusted *F* tests are identical.

```{r}
#| code-summary: "Latin-square ANOVA on group × period means (16 values per outcome)"

ls_specs <- tribble(
  ~key,          ~data,            ~resp,
  "graz_day",    "behavior_day",   "grazing",
  "other_day",   "behavior_day",   "other",
  "lying_day",   "behavior_day",   "lying",
  "rum_day",     "behavior_day",   "ruminating_tot",
  "stand_day",   "behavior_day",   "standing",
  "graz_night",  "behavior_night", "grazing",
  "other_night", "behavior_night", "other",
  "lying_night", "behavior_night", "lying",
  "rum_night",   "behavior_night", "ruminating_tot",
  "stand_night", "behavior_night", "standing",
  "events",      "events",         "events",
  "intake",      "intake",         "intake_per_animal",
  "duration",    "drinking",       "log(drinking_time_s)",
  "sips",        "drinking",       "sips",
  "sip_rate",    "drinking",       "sip_rate_s"
)

# One mean per group × period (the experimental unit)
gp_means <- function(data, resp) {
  get(data) %>%
    mutate(.y = !!rlang::parse_expr(resp)) %>%
    group_by(group, period, treatment, shade, water) %>%
    summarise(y = mean(.y, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop")
}

ls_p <- map_dfr(seq_len(nrow(ls_specs)), function(i) {
  s  <- ls_specs[i, ]
  gp <- gp_means(s$data, s$resp)
  a_trt  <- anova(lm(y ~ period + group + treatment, data = gp))
  a_fact <- anova(lm(y ~ period + group + shade * water, data = gp))
  tibble(
    key        = s$key,
    n_units    = nrow(gp),
    df_error   = a_trt["Residuals", "Df"],
    ls_trt     = a_trt["treatment", "Pr(>F)"],
    ls_shade   = a_fact["shade", "Pr(>F)"],
    ls_water   = a_fact["water", "Pr(>F)"],
    ls_int     = a_fact["shade:water", "Pr(>F)"]
  )
})

# Mixed-model counterparts: treatment F (behavior treatment models) and the
# factorial joint tests (Table 46)
trt_models <- list(
  graz_day    = model_graz_day_trat,    other_day   = model_other_day_trat,
  lying_day   = model_lying_day_trat,   rum_day     = model_rum_day_trat,
  stand_day   = model_stand_day_trat,   graz_night  = model_graze_night_trat,
  other_night = model_other_night_trat, lying_night = model_lying_night_trat,
  rum_night   = model_rum_night_trat,   stand_night = model_stand_night_trat
)
trt_labels <- c(graz_night = "model_graze_night_trat")

mm_p <- fact_jt %>%
  select(key, term, p) %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = term, values_from = p) %>%
  transmute(key, mm_shade = shade, mm_water = water, mm_int = `shade:water`) %>%
  left_join(
    tibble(key = names(trt_models),
           mm_trt = map_dbl(trt_models, ~ anova(.)["treatment", "Pr(>F)"])),
    by = "key"
  )

# group:period variance ≈ 0 in the treatment or factorial mixed model
gp_zero_models <- model_log$model[str_detect(model_log$action, "group:period variance ≈ 0")]
gp_zero <- map_lgl(ls_specs$key, function(k) {
  trt_lab <- if (k %in% names(trt_labels)) trt_labels[[k]] else paste0("model_", k, "_trat")
  any(str_detect(gp_zero_models, fixed(paste0("factorial_", k)))) ||
    trt_lab %in% gp_zero_models ||
    (k == "events" && "model_events (Poisson)" %in% gp_zero_models) ||
    (k == "intake" && "model_intake" %in% gp_zero_models)
})

eu_compare <- ls_p %>%
  left_join(mm_p, by = "key") %>%
  mutate(gp_zero = gp_zero[match(key, ls_specs$key)]) %>%
  left_join(fact_specs %>% select(key, Outcome, Daypart), by = "key")

# Significance (at 0.05) that differs between the two analyses
eu_flips <- eu_compare %>%
  select(key, Outcome, Daypart, gp_zero, ls_trt:ls_int, mm_shade:mm_trt) %>%
  pivot_longer(c(starts_with("ls_"), starts_with("mm_")),
               names_to = c("method", "term"), names_sep = "_") %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = method, values_from = value) %>%
  filter(!is.na(mm), !is.na(ls), (mm < 0.05) != (ls < 0.05)) %>%
  mutate(term = recode(term, trt = "Treatment", shade = "Shade", water = "Water",
                       int = "Shade × Water"))

p_cell <- function(x) ifelse(is.na(x), "—", ifelse(x < 0.001, "< 0.001", formatC(x, format = "f", digits = 3)))

eu_compare %>%
  transmute(
    Outcome = paste0(Outcome, if_else(gp_zero, " †", "")), Daypart,
    `Treatment: LS` = p_cell(ls_trt), `Treatment: MM` = p_cell(mm_trt),
    `Shade: LS` = p_cell(ls_shade),   `Shade: MM` = p_cell(mm_shade),
    `Water: LS` = p_cell(ls_water),   `Water: MM` = p_cell(mm_water),
    `S × W: LS` = p_cell(ls_int),     `S × W: MM` = p_cell(mm_int)
  ) %>%
  kbl(caption = "Table 47a. P-values from the Latin-square ANOVA on group × period means (LS; 16 units, 6 error df) and from the mixed models (MM; treatment F from the treatment models, shade/water/interaction from Table 46).") %>%
  kable_styling(bootstrap_options = c("striped", "hover"), full_width = FALSE) %>%
  row_spec(0, background = "#2C4A2E", color = "white", bold = TRUE) %>%
  row_spec(which(eu_compare$gp_zero), bold = TRUE) %>%
  footnote(general = c(
    paste0("† Bold rows: the group:period variance was estimated as ≈ 0 in the treatment and/or factorial mixed model, ",
           "so its denominator df default to the observation level and its tests are liberal; the LS column is the more conservative test."),
    "MM treatment F is available only for the behavior outcomes; the drinking outcomes were modelled by water (Section 5) and in the factorial models."
  ))
```

```{r}
#| code-summary: "Tests whose significance at 0.05 differs between the two analyses"

if (nrow(eu_flips)) {
  eu_flips %>%
    transmute(Outcome = paste0(Outcome, if_else(gp_zero, " †", "")), Daypart,
              Term = term, `p (LS, group × period)` = p_cell(ls), `p (mixed model)` = p_cell(mm)) %>%
    kbl(caption = "Table 47b. Tests significant at 0.05 in one analysis but not the other.") %>%
    kable_styling(bootstrap_options = c("striped", "hover"), full_width = FALSE) %>%
    row_spec(0, background = "#2C4A2E", color = "white", bold = TRUE)
} else {
  cat("All tests agree at the 0.05 level.")
}
```

# 9 · Model Fitting Notes and Residual Diagnostics

## 9.1 · Convergence and singularity

Every animal-level model includes `(1 | group:period)`, because group × period (16 units) is the experimental unit. Models that did not converge or were singular were refitted with the `bobyqa` optimizer; if still singular, random terms with zero variance were dropped (never `group:period`).

```{r}
#| code-summary: "Convergence / singularity log for all LMMs and GLMMs"

model_log %>%
  rename(Model = model, Status = status, Action = action, `Final random-effect variances` = final) %>%
  kbl(caption = "Table 48. Convergence and singularity checks for all fitted models.") %>%
  kable_styling(bootstrap_options = c("striped", "hover"), full_width = FALSE) %>%
  row_spec(0, background = "#2C4A2E", color = "white", bold = TRUE)
```

## 9.2 · Residual diagnostics

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="Residual diagnostics (click to expand)"}

```{r}
#| code-summary: "LMMs — residuals vs fitted values"
#| fig-cap: "Figure 25. Residuals vs fitted values for the main LMMs."
#| fig-width: 11
#| fig-height: 9

diag_lmms <- list(
  "Grazing (day)"          = model_graz_day_trat,
  "Other (day)"            = model_other_day_trat,
  "Lying (day)"            = model_lying_day_trat,
  "Ruminating (day)"       = model_rum_day_trat,
  "Standing (day)"         = model_stand_day_trat,
  "Grazing (night)"        = model_graze_night_trat,
  "Other (night)"          = model_other_night_trat,
  "Lying (night)"          = model_lying_night_trat,
  "Ruminating (night)"     = model_rum_night_trat,
  "Standing (night)"       = model_stand_night_trat,
  "Shade use (prop.)"      = model_shade_prop,
  "Water intake"           = model_intake,
  "log drinking duration"  = model_drink_time,
  "Sip rate"               = model_sip_rate
)

diag_df <- imap_dfr(diag_lmms, ~ tibble(model = .y, fitted = fitted(.x), resid = resid(.x))) %>%
  mutate(model = factor(model, levels = names(diag_lmms)))

ggplot(diag_df, aes(fitted, resid)) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, color = "#6B6B6B", linetype = "dashed") +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.15, size = 0.6, color = "#2C4A2E") +
  geom_smooth(method = "loess", formula = y ~ x, se = FALSE, color = "#C8A84B", linewidth = 0.8) +
  facet_wrap(~ model, scales = "free", ncol = 4) +
  labs(x = "Fitted", y = "Residual") +
  theme_ws()
```

```{r}
#| code-summary: "LMMs — normal QQ plots of residuals"
#| fig-cap: "Figure 26. Normal QQ plots of the residuals of the main LMMs."
#| fig-width: 11
#| fig-height: 9

ggplot(diag_df, aes(sample = resid)) +
  stat_qq(alpha = 0.2, size = 0.6, color = "#2C4A2E") +
  stat_qq_line(color = "#C8A84B") +
  facet_wrap(~ model, scales = "free", ncol = 4) +
  labs(x = "Theoretical quantiles", y = "Sample quantiles") +
  theme_ws()
```

```{r}
#| code-summary: "GLMMs — DHARMa simulated residuals (drinking events)"
#| fig-cap: "Figure 27. DHARMa simulated-residual diagnostics for the Poisson GLMM of daily drinking events."
#| fig-width: 10
#| fig-height: 4.5

set.seed(2024)
dharma_events <- simulateResiduals(model_events, n = 1000)
plot(dharma_events)
```

```{r}
#| code-summary: "GLMMs — DHARMa dispersion and zero-inflation tests (drinking events)"

dharma_tests <- function(sim, label) {
  disp <- testDispersion(sim, plot = FALSE)
  zi   <- testZeroInflation(sim, plot = FALSE)
  unif <- testUniformity(sim, plot = FALSE)
  tibble(
    Model = label,
    `Dispersion ratio (sim.)` = round(unname(disp$statistic), 3),
    `p (dispersion)`          = round(disp$p.value, 4),
    `Zero-inflation ratio`    = round(unname(zi$statistic), 3),
    `p (zero-inflation)`      = round(zi$p.value, 4),
    `p (KS uniformity)`       = round(unif$p.value, 4)
  )
}

dharma_tbl <- dharma_tests(dharma_events, "Drinking events (Poisson)")

if (events_underdispersed) {
  set.seed(2024)
  dharma_events_gp <- simulateResiduals(model_events_gp, n = 1000)
  dharma_tbl <- bind_rows(dharma_tbl, dharma_tests(dharma_events_gp, "Drinking events (generalized Poisson)"))
}
```

```{r}
#| code-summary: "GLMMs — DHARMa simulated residuals (sips per event)"
#| fig-cap: "Figure 28. DHARMa simulated-residual diagnostics for the GLMM of sips per drinking event."
#| fig-width: 10
#| fig-height: 4.5

set.seed(2024)
dharma_sips <- simulateResiduals(model_sips, n = 1000)
plot(dharma_sips)

dharma_tbl <- bind_rows(dharma_tbl, dharma_tests(dharma_sips, paste("Sips per event —", sips_family)))

dharma_tbl %>%
  kbl(caption = "Table 49. DHARMa tests on simulated residuals for the count GLMMs.") %>%
  kable_styling(bootstrap_options = c("striped", "hover"), full_width = FALSE) %>%
  row_spec(0, background = "#2C4A2E", color = "white", bold = TRUE)
```

```{r}
#| include: false
#| code-summary: "Prepare values and CLD letters for the Results section"

get_emm <- function(emm, level) round(emm$means$Mean[emm$means$Level == level], 3)

get_p <- function(emm, idx = 1) fmt_p(emm$contrasts$`p-value`[idx])

# Omnibus F test for treatment (Satterthwaite) from a treatment model
get_trt_p <- function(model) anova(model)["treatment", "Pr(>F)"]

get_cld <- function(model, factor) {
  emm <- emmeans(model, as.formula(paste("~", factor)))
  cld_df <- multcomp::cld(emm, Letters = letters, adjust = "tukey", reversed = TRUE)
  cld_df <- as.data.frame(cld_df)
  nms <- names(cld_df)
  data.frame(
    Level   = cld_df[[nms[1]]],
    Letters = trimws(cld_df[[nms[length(nms)]]])
  )
}

           list(mean = ~ mean(.), sd = ~ sd(.)),
```

## Behavioral Activity Patterns

### Daytime Behavior

With group × period as the experimental unit, treatment affected daytime `r and_list(p_list(day_sig, "day"))`, but not `r and_list(p_list(day_ns, "day"))` (Table 2; F tests with Satterthwaite df). Pure grazing was highest in `r uni(extreme_trt("grazing", "Daytime"))` (`r desc_val("grazing", "Daytime", extreme_trt("grazing", "Daytime"))`% of scans) and lowest in `r uni(extreme_trt("grazing", "Daytime", which.min))` (`r desc_val("grazing", "Daytime", extreme_trt("grazing", "Daytime", which.min))`%). Standing was lowest in `r uni(extreme_trt("standing", "Daytime", which.min))` (`r desc_val("standing", "Daytime", extreme_trt("standing", "Daytime", which.min))`%) and highest in `r uni(extreme_trt("standing", "Daytime"))` (`r desc_val("standing", "Daytime", extreme_trt("standing", "Daytime"))`%). Other behaviors were a small part of the budget (`r min(round(budget_desc$other_mean[budget_desc$daypart == "Daytime"], 1))`–`r max(round(budget_desc$other_mean[budget_desc$daypart == "Daytime"], 1))`% of daytime scans). Within each column of Table 2, values sharing a letter do not differ significantly (Tukey-adjusted, p > 0.05).

**Table 2.** Behavioral budget (% of scans) by treatment and period. Values are mean ± SD across animals. Different letters within a column and period indicate significant differences between treatments (Tukey-adjusted, p < 0.05). S+W+ = Shade + ad libitum water; S+W− = Shade + restricted water; S−W+ = No shade + ad libitum water; S−W− = No shade + restricted water.

```{r}
#| code-summary: "Table 2 — behavior budget with day and night rows"

build_cell <- function(desc, cld, behavior, daypart, level) {
  row <- desc %>% filter(treatment == level, daypart == !!daypart)
  m <- round(row[[paste0(behavior, "_mean")]], 1)
  s <- round(row[[paste0(behavior, "_sd")]], 1)
  l <- cld %>% filter(Level == level) %>% pull(Letters)
  paste0(m, " ± ", s, " ", l)
}

build_rows <- function(daypart, cld_graz, cld_other, cld_lying, cld_rum, cld_stand) {
  tibble(
    Treatment          = c("S+W+", "S+W−", "S−W+", "S−W−"),
    Period             = daypart,
    `Grazing`          = map_chr(levels_vec, ~ build_cell(budget_desc, cld_graz,  "grazing",        daypart, .x)),
    `Other`            = map_chr(levels_vec, ~ build_cell(budget_desc, cld_other, "other",          daypart, .x)),
    `Lying`            = map_chr(levels_vec, ~ build_cell(budget_desc, cld_lying, "lying",          daypart, .x)),
    `Ruminating`       = map_chr(levels_vec, ~ build_cell(budget_desc, cld_rum,   "ruminating_tot", daypart, .x)),
    `Standing`         = map_chr(levels_vec, ~ build_cell(budget_desc, cld_stand, "standing",       daypart, .x))
  )
}

levels_vec <- c("S+W+", "S+W-", "S-W+", "S-W-")

table2 <- bind_rows(
  build_rows("Daytime",   cld_graz_day,   cld_other_day,   cld_lying_day,   cld_rum_day,   cld_stand_day),
  build_rows("Nighttime", cld_graz_night, cld_other_night, cld_lying_night, cld_rum_night, cld_stand_night)
)

table2 %>%
  kbl(caption = "Table 2. Behavioral budget (% of scans) by treatment and period (mean ± SD).",
      align = "llccccc", linesep = "") %>%
  kable_styling(bootstrap_options = c("striped", "hover"), full_width = FALSE) %>%
  row_spec(0, background = "#2C4A2E", color = "white", bold = TRUE) %>%
  pack_rows("Daytime", 1, 4, background = "#F5F0E8", bold = TRUE) %>%
  pack_rows("Nighttime", 5, 8, background = "#F5F0E8", bold = TRUE) %>%
  footnote(general = "Grazing = pure grazing; Other = behaviors outside the ethogram categories (previously added to grazing). Lying and standing are postures; ruminating is in any posture and overlaps with both. Different letters within a column and period indicate significant differences (Tukey-adjusted, p < 0.05).")
```

In the single-factor models, shaded animals (S+) grazed `r direction(graz_day_shade_emm)` during the day than unshaded animals (S−; p `r graz_p_shade`), lay down `r direction(lying_day_shade_emm)` (p `r lying_p_shade`) and stood `r direction(stand_day_shade_emm)` (p `r stand_p_shade`). Water-restricted animals (W−) grazed `r direction(graz_day_water_emm, "less", "more")` than W+ animals (p `r graz_p_water`) and stood `r direction(stand_day_water_emm, "less", "more")` (p `r stand_p_water`).

The factorial models (Table 46) separate these effects. For daytime grazing, water had a strong main effect (p `r fact_p("graz_day", "water")`), shade a weaker one (p `r fact_p("graz_day", "shade")`), and the two interacted (p `r fact_p("graz_day", "shade:water")`): shade increased grazing when water was available (S+W+ vs S−W+: p `r se_p("graz_day", "| water = W+")`) but not under water restriction (S+W− vs S−W−: p `r se_p("graz_day", "| water = W-")`), so water restriction removed the grazing benefit of shade. Daytime standing was affected by both shade (p `r fact_p("stand_day", "shade")`) and water (p `r fact_p("stand_day", "water")`) without interaction (p `r fact_p("stand_day", "shade:water")`).

### Nocturnal Grazing

At night, treatment affected `r and_list(p_list(night_sig, "night"))`, but not `r and_list(p_list(night_ns, "night"))`. Nocturnal grazing was `r if (graze_night_shade_emm$contrasts$Estimate[1] > 0) "higher" else "lower"` in shaded than unshaded animals (p `r ngraz_p_shade`), whereas water access alone did not predict it (p `r ngraz_p_water`). Among individual treatments, `r uni(extreme_trt("grazing", "Nighttime"))` showed the highest nocturnal grazing (`r desc_val("grazing", "Nighttime", extreme_trt("grazing", "Nighttime"))`% of scans). In the factorial model the shade × water interaction for nocturnal grazing was p `r fact_p("graz_night", "shade:water")`: shade increased nocturnal grazing under water restriction (S+W− vs S−W−: p `r se_p("graz_night", "| water = W-")`) but not with free water (p `r se_p("graz_night", "| water = W+")`), consistent with compensatory night grazing in S+W−. Nocturnal lying was highest in `r uni(extreme_trt("lying", "Nighttime"))` (`r desc_val("lying", "Nighttime", extreme_trt("lying", "Nighttime"))`%; shade effect in the factorial model p `r fact_p("lying_night", "shade")`). The full 24-hour behavioral profile for each treatment is shown in Figure 1, and the day-to-night shift in grazing is illustrated in Figures 2 and 3.

```{r}
#| code-summary: "Figure 1 — 24-hour grazing and lying profile (static)"
#| fig-cap: "Figure 1. Mean grazing and lying scans per hour across the 24-hour cycle by treatment. The vertical dashed line at 12.5 marks the daytime–nighttime transition (19:00h). The red dotted line at 12:00h marks the scheduled watering time for W− treatments."
#| fig-width: 8
#| fig-height: 6
#| fig-align: center

full_ts <- behavior %>%
  group_by(treatment, hour, clock_time) %>%
  summarise(
    Grazing = mean(grazing, na.rm = TRUE),
    Lying   = mean(lying,   na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  pivot_longer(c(Grazing, Lying), names_to = "behavior", values_to = "mean") %>%
  mutate(clock_time = factor(clock_time, levels = clock_labels))

ggplot(full_ts,
       aes(x = hour, y = mean, color = behavior, group = behavior)) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 12.5, linetype = "dashed",
             color = "#6B6B6B", linewidth = 0.7) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 5.5, linetype = "dotted",
             color = "#CC0000", linewidth = 0.8) +
  annotate("text", x = 6.0, y = max(full_ts$mean, na.rm = TRUE) * 0.96,
           label = "Water (W−)", hjust = 0, size = 3, color = "#CC0000") +
  annotate("text", x = 6.5,  y = max(full_ts$mean, na.rm = TRUE) * 0.88,
           label = "Daytime", hjust = 0.5, size = 3, color = "#6B6B6B") +
  annotate("text", x = 18.5, y = max(full_ts$mean, na.rm = TRUE) * 0.88,
           label = "Nighttime", hjust = 0.5, size = 3, color = "#6B6B6B") +
  geom_line(linewidth = 1) +
  geom_point(size = 1.8) +
  scale_color_manual(values = c("Grazing" = "#2C4A2E", "Lying" = "#4A7FA5")) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = 1:24, labels = unname(clock_labels)) +
  facet_wrap(~ treatment, nrow = 2) +
  labs(x = "Clock time", y = "Mean scans / h", color = "Behavior") +
  theme_ws(angle_x = 45)
```

```{r}
                  ylim = c(min(graz_quad$night_grazing) - 0.05,
                           max(graz_quad$night_grazing) + 0.1)) +
  labs(x = "Daytime grazing (scans / h)",
       y = "Nocturnal grazing (scans / h)") +
  theme_ws() +
  theme(legend.position = "none")
```

## Drinking Behavior and Water Intake

Counting every animal-day (including `r events_n_zero` animal-days without drinking), ad libitum animals (W+) drank `r events_rr`× as often as restricted animals (`r events_rate_wp` vs `r events_rate_wm` events/animal/day; rate ratio = `r events_rr`; p `r events_p_text`). The Poisson model was underdispersed (dispersion ratio = `r overdisp_ratio`); `r events_gp_txt`. Daily water intake per animal was `r intake_wp` L in W+ and `r intake_wm` L in W− (difference = `r intake_diff` L; p `r intake_p_text`), `r if (intake_p < 0.05) "a significant difference" else "a difference that was not significant with group × period as the experimental unit"`. Within bouts, W− animals took `r if (sips_p < 0.05) "more" else "a similar number of"` sips per event (`r sips_wm` vs `r sips_wp`; `r sips_family`, Poisson dispersion ratio = `r sips_disp`; p `r sips_p_text`), and their bouts were `r if (dt_p < 0.05) "longer" else "not significantly longer"` (geometric mean `r dt_wm` s vs `r dt_wp` s; ratio = `r dt_ratio`; p `r dt_p_text`), at the same sip rate (W+: `r sr_wp` sips/s; W−: `r sr_wm` sips/s; p `r sr_p_text`).

```{r}
#| code-summary: "Figure 4 — drinking events per animal per day (static)"

ggplot(events, aes(x = treatment, color = treatment)) +
  geom_jitter(aes(y = events), width = 0.15, alpha = 0.45,
              size = 2.5, shape = 16) +
  geom_pointrange(
    data = events_summary_plot,
    aes(y = mean, ymin = mean - se, ymax = mean + se),
    shape = 18, size = 0.9, linewidth = 1.1, color = "black"
  ) +
  scale_color_manual(values = pal_treatment) +
  labs(x = "Treatment", y = "Drinking events / animal / day", color = NULL) +
  theme_ws() +
  theme(legend.position = "none")
```

## Shade Area Use

Among S+ animals, those with restricted water (S+W−) spent `r if (shade_p < 0.05) "a significantly greater" else "a similar"` proportion of daytime scans in shade compared with ad libitum animals (`r scales::percent(prop_spwm, accuracy = 0.1)` vs `r scales::percent(prop_spwp, accuracy = 0.1)`; p `r shade_p_text`), despite having access to the same silvopastoral area (Figure 7). The difference came mainly from the morning: between `r shade_morning_span`, S+W− animals were in shade `r shade_diff_morning` percentage points more often than S+W+ on average, whereas between `r shade_afternoon_span` the two treatments differed by only `r shade_diff_afternoon` points on average. Shade use peaked at `r shade_peak_hour`h. The `r paste0(clock_labels[shade_excluded_hours], "h", collapse = " and ")` scan blocks were excluded for both treatments because S+W− animals were in the trough corridor (recorded as sun) during watering. This shows a trade-off: water restriction made animals leave shaded areas during hot hours.

```{r}
#| code-summary: "Figure 7 — shade use across the day (static)"
#| fig-cap: "Figure 7. Mean proportion of daytime scans in shade by hour (S+ treatments). Ribbons = ±1 SD. Red dashed lines mark the W− watering blocks (12:00h and 17:00h), excluded from the analysis for both treatments."
#| fig-width: 7
#| fig-height: 4.5
#| fig-align: center

shade_hour <- shade_model_data %>%
  mutate(hour_int = as.integer(as.character(hour))) %>%
  group_by(treatment, hour_int) %>%
  summarise(
    mean = mean(prop_shade, na.rm = TRUE),
    sd   = sd(prop_shade,   na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  mutate(clock = factor(scan_to_clock(hour_int), levels = day_labels))

ggplot(shade_hour,
       aes(x = clock, y = mean,
           color = treatment, fill = treatment, group = treatment)) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = pmax(mean - sd, 0), ymax = pmin(mean + sd, 1)),
              alpha = 0.15, color = NA) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = shade_excluded_hours, linetype = "dashed",
             color = "#CC0000", linewidth = 0.9) +
  annotate("text", x = shade_excluded_hours + 0.15, y = 0.75, hjust = 0, vjust = 0, size = 3,
           color = "#CC0000", label = "Water offering time") +
  geom_line(linewidth = 1.2) +
  geom_point(size = 2.5) +
  scale_color_manual(values = c("S+W+" = "#2C4A2E", "S+W-" = "#4A7FA5")) +
  scale_fill_manual( values = c("S+W+" = "#2C4A2E", "S+W-" = "#4A7FA5")) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::percent, limits = c(0, 1)) +
  scale_x_discrete(drop = FALSE) +
  labs(x = "Clock time", y = "Proportion of scans in shade",
       color = "Treatment", fill = "Treatment") +
  theme_ws(angle_x = 45)
```

```{r}
#| code-summary: "Figure 8 — location distribution across the day (static, stacked area)"
#| fig-cap: "Figure 8. Proportion of daytime scans by location for S+ treatments. Red dashed line marks 12:00h."
#| fig-width: 8
#| fig-height: 4.5
#| fig-align: center

shade_use_static <- behavior_raw %>%
  filter(
    treatment %in% c("S+W+", "S+W-"),
    location  %in% c("sun", "shade", "sun_between_trees"),
    hour <= 12
  ) %>%
  group_by(treatment, hour, clock_time, location) %>%
  summarise(total_scans = sum(total, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop") %>%
  group_by(treatment, hour, clock_time) %>%
  mutate(
    prop       = total_scans / sum(total_scans),
    clock_time = factor(clock_time, levels = day_labels)
  ) %>%
  ungroup()

annotation_df <- data.frame(
  treatment  = factor("S+W-", levels = c("S+W+", "S+W-")),
  clock_time = factor("12:00", levels = levels(shade_use_static$clock_time)),
  prop       = 0.75,
  label      = "Water offering time"
)

line_df <- data.frame(
  treatment  = factor("S+W-", levels = c("S+W+", "S+W-")),
  x          = 6,
  xend       = 6,
  y          = 0,
  yend       = 1
)

ggplot(shade_use_static,
       aes(x = clock_time, y = prop, fill = location, group = location)) +
  geom_area(position = "fill", alpha = 0.85) +
  geom_segment(data = line_df,
               aes(x = x, xend = xend, y = y, yend = yend),
               inherit.aes = FALSE,
               linetype = "dashed", color = "#CC0000", linewidth = 1) +
  geom_text(data = annotation_df,
            aes(x = clock_time, y = prop, label = label),
            inherit.aes = FALSE,
            hjust = 0, vjust = 0, size = 3, color = "#CC0000",
            nudge_x = 0.5) +
  scale_fill_manual(
    values = pal_location,
    labels = c("Sun", "Shade", "Sun between trees")
  ) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::percent) +
  facet_wrap(~ treatment) +

       y = "Proportion of scans", fill = "Location") +

```
## Sensitivity to the Experimental Unit

```{r}
#| include: false
#| code-summary: "Values for the experimental-unit sensitivity text"

eu_label <- function(outcome, daypart) {
  o <- tolower(str_remove(outcome, " \\(.*\\)$"))
  if_else(daypart == "24 h", o, paste(tolower(daypart), o))
}
# Treatment F (behavior only) plus shade, water and shade × water per outcome
eu_n_tests <- sum(!is.na(eu_compare$mm_trt)) + 3 * nrow(eu_compare)
eu_n_flip  <- nrow(eu_flips)
eu_flip_txt <- eu_flips %>%
  mutate(txt = paste0(tolower(term), " for ", eu_label(Outcome, Daypart),
                      " (LS p ", fmt_p(ls), "; mixed model p ", fmt_p(mm), ")")) %>%
  pull(txt) %>% and_list()
eu_gp_zero_txt <- eu_compare %>% filter(gp_zero) %>%
  mutate(lab = eu_label(Outcome, Daypart)) %>% pull(lab) %>% and_list()
```

Reducing each outcome to its `r eu_compare$n_units[1]` group × period means and analysing them as a Latin square (`r eu_compare$df_error[1]` error df) gave the same conclusion at the 0.05 level for `r eu_n_tests - eu_n_flip` of `r eu_n_tests` tests (Table 47a). `r if (eu_n_flip) paste0("The ", eu_n_flip, " that differed were ", eu_flip_txt, " (Table 47b).") else "No test changed."` The group:period variance was ≈ 0 in the mixed models for `r eu_gp_zero_txt`; for these outcomes the Latin-square test on group × period means is the more conservative reference.
